lots.title: 25112 Library Services Engage, Design and Fit out Contract - Ely Library
lots.description: Single-lot design-and-build contract for the refresh of Ely Library: design engagement with library staff and the Friends group, supply of library furniture, signage and graphics, and replacement flooring/carpet throughout the main library footprint. Scope covers the core library footprint of just under 850sqm on the ground and first floors of the Cloisters precinct, Ely. The successful bidder produces the final design post-award (bidders are not required to produce a final design at tender stage). Out of scope: the 2022-refurbished main entrance and stairway, provision of power/data, and specialist IT (public PCs, self-service machines), which are delivered by the Authority's IT and electrical contractors.
requirements: Design-and-build delivery: produce design principles, methodology and proposals, then supply and install agreed furniture and fittings within budget (§1.1, §1.2).
Cost of design and stakeholder engagement is included within the contract budget; no final design is required at tender stage (§1.3).
Design engagement must include, as a minimum, a site visit, engagement with staff and the Friends group, and at least one feedback round on a first design (§1.4, §3.9).

Respect the existing 2022-refurbished main entrance/stairway and exclude power/data provision and specialist IT (public PCs, self-service machines); these remain with the Authority's IT and electrical contractors (§2.1, §2.2).
Design must remain sympathetic to the character of the building while enhancing audience appeal (§3.6).
Embed sustainability in design approach, methodology and furniture, including environmental credentials and longevity (must still look fresh 5-10 years on) (§3.7, §3.8).
Deliver a modern, calming, flexible and adaptable space with an exceptional visitor experience (§4.1, §4.2, §4.3).
Library must be fully accessible and as dementia- and autism-friendly as possible (§4.4).
Signage and graphics must be treated as integral design elements, not secondary (§4.5).
Replace carpet throughout the main library footprint (§4.6).

Deliver distinct internal zones within the single open-plan space (Children's library, Study, Adult shelving, IT & Printing, Bespoke staff desk, Self-service, Events, Social seating, First Floor Lobby), coordinating thoroughfares and sightlines from the main desk (§5, §5.11).

Children's library: storage for craft/activity materials; standing staff desk near the entrance; seating for storytime; desk space for colouring/homework with power considered (installed out of contract); refreshed or replaced interactive picture book stand; maintain 38 shelves junior fiction, 62 shelves non-fiction and 10 kinder boxes, with options to enhance existing Cantilibra shelving (36 walled, 52 static, 16 wheeled) and an improved face-out display (§5.1.3 - §5.1.8).

Study provision: increase dedicated desks from 12 to 18, with at least 10 having access to power; flexibility to combine desks into group seating; overhead-power installation is under consideration and may be tendered separately by the Authority (§5.2.2 - §5.2.6).

Adult shelving: enhance existing shelving where possible to reduce waste and help define zones; indicative shelving is 210 adult fiction (incl. large print and spoken word), 120 adult non-fiction, 18 young adult, 20 local studies; provide a distinct Young Adult zone (§5.3.3 - §5.3.5).

IT & Printing: accommodate six public PCs with power and data; at least one PC desk must be wheelchair-accessible/height-adjustable; MFD sited near staff desk; maintain privacy between PC users (§5.4.2 - §5.4.6).

Bespoke staff desk: two staff PC stations with RFID pads, each with three power points and one data port; one data port for a Teams phone; one power for till; two additional power points for iPad/device charging; behind-desk storage (tambour cupboard or similar); in-desk light-stationery storage and lockable unit for secure iPad charging (§5.5.1 - §5.5.8).
Self-service: accommodate three Lyngsoe Phoenix devices, each with a double-sided trolley, plus two dump bins shared across the three (§5.6.2, §5.6.3).

Events space: support flexible use for groups such as the ~25-person veterans group, with sociable tables, some storage, and scope to flex the whole library for larger events such as 'The Library Presents' (§5.7).
Social seating: hotel-lobby-like soft-seating area for 8-10 people with a table for drinks, and accommodate the Warm Hub trolley with regular hot-drinks access (§5.8).

Flooring: replace throughout the main library space; must be easy to maintain; darker colours preferred to mask spills from the Warm Hub, teen and children's zones; provide floor protection or alternative covering where spills are concentrated (§5.9.2 - §5.9.4).
First Floor Lobby: add a bar-stool-height desk and seating with power supply; provide a poster/leaflet information display solution, ideally space-efficient (§5.10.2, §5.10.3).
Design must respect thoroughfares (toilets, meeting rooms, fire exits) and maintain clear sightlines from the main desk, avoiding hidden areas (§5.11).
All on-site work requires pre-approved Risk Assessments and Method Statements specific to the first-floor location and limited delivery windows, submitted in good time for feedback (§6.2, §7.1.a).
Coordinate with the Authority's IT services and core maintenance contractors, including into the bidder-managed project plan (§6.3, §7.2).
Access constraints: rear access with small goods lift and limited availability; large deliveries likely via the front pedestrianised entrance, coordinated with the landlord (§7.4).

Implementation/Mobilisation: initial onboarding with library, property, compliance teams and design consultants; site visit and stakeholder engagement; design delivery with feedback cycle and contract-management meetings covering performance, issues, material changes and pricing changes (§8.1 - §8.5).

Indicative project timetable (to be finalised at award): site visit and engagement 6-20 July 2026; design draft 20 July-3 Aug 2026; engagement on design 3-10 Aug 2026; final design draft 10-31 Aug 2026; sign-off 4 Sep 2026; order of furniture 7 Sep 2026; fit-out delivery and install 2 Nov - 20 Dec 2026; training, sign-off and handover 4-8 Jan 2027; 12-month defects period from handover (§9, Project/Contract timetable table).

Provide robust carbon-reduction strategies: reduce waste (packaging/construction), transport (consolidated deliveries, local employees), re-use or re-purpose materials (salvage existing furniture) and ensure long product life (§10.1, §10.2).
Provide warranty details as part of the bid, especially under question 2 on sustainability (§10.3).
Provide a minimum 12-month defects period after handover (§10.4).
Subcontracting is permitted; it must be declared in the bid, and all sub-contractors must abide by procurement and contract requirements (§11).

At end of contract provide required documentation (materials/equipment used) in an agreed format, deliver in-person handover training, and update documentation during the defects stage as necessary (§12).
Comply with the Modern Slavery Act with sufficient policies, procedures and systems (§13.1).
Comply with the Equality Act and all EDI regulations with sufficient policies, procedures and systems (§14.1).
Comply with UK GDPR; any breach (suspected or otherwise) must be reported to the Council immediately and within 72 hours (§15.1, §15.2).
Follow the ITT section 4.1 purchase-order and invoicing processes; payments tied to milestones agreed with the Contract Manager; no pre-payment or deposit will be made (§16.1 - §16.4).

warnings.message: This specification document identifies two scored criteria (sustainability under question 2, case studies from similar work) but does not disclose numeric weightings or the full evaluation matrix. Full evaluation criteria and weightings are expected to be in the ITT document, not this appendix.

CPV codes 39155000-3 (Library furniture) and 79932000-6 (Interior design services) are derived from the notice-level process context and map cleanly to the §1.1 scope language ('design, furniture, signage, and carpet'). No CPV codes are literally quoted within the specification text itself.

This Appendix 4 specification covers a single contract lot; internal 'zones' in §5 (Children's, Study, Adult shelving, IT, Staff desk, Self-service, Events, Social, Lobby) are functional zones, not separate bidding lots. Existing notice_lots row (lot_number=1) is preserved.

Provision of power and data is explicitly out of scope (delivered by the Authority's IT and electrical contractors); bidder remains responsible for coordination and for furniture/desks that accommodate the declared power/data counts.

Minor OCR/typographic anomalies present in source markdown (e.g. 'Lynsgoe' for 'Lyngsoe', 'Morden' for 'Modern', 'interesting' for 'interested') were normalised in extracted output but may affect downstream text matching against source anchors.
